title: Integrated Planning Act appeal 3-08-042: extension to a building with earlier fire-engineered work; fire engineering scope approved without a completed referral process (Toowoomba region)
jurisdiction: Queensland, Australia. COMPARATIVE TEST ONLY: not Alberta; no Alberta applicability asserted.

document_type: Integrated Planning Act 1997 appeal decision (Tribunal), Queensland
document_date: Decision dated 6 Aug 2008 (PDF p. 3); hearing 21 Jul 2008 (p. 1)

facts.text: QFRS (Toowoomba region) appealed under IPA s 4.2.10 the council's approval of a scope of work described in a fire engineering report, alleging that due process was not fully applied.

The tribunal confirmed the QFRS appeal against the development application decision notice dated 14 Mar 2008, and directed stakeholders to complete the due process needed to close off outstanding fire-safety matters.
The subject building had a previous approval for fire-engineering work; an extension was then proposed, and the fire engineering report for the new work relied on alternative solutions.
The decision notice treated the report's scope as acceptable, and the notice records no evidence that stakeholders had agreed the alternative solutions.
The tribunal noted an additional fire wall that was not shown on the submitted plans, and an escape route into an existing external easement.
The tribunal said an agreed outcome on fire-engineering matters must be reached to deliver an acceptable result.
